messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-hotpath-pool-3 saturated, queue depth rising > 12k, sustained 429 rate ~50% in last 1m. Autoscaler reported scale-up rejected. https://ops.internal/alerts/2098765432
sre-jen: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking autoscaler events
matt_almond: seeing same — tokenbucket refill for tier 'standard' dropped to 0 r/s after the recent rate-policy push. probable misassign of routing keys to tiers.
leo_ops: tagging @nikki_pm for customer impact — which customers are seeing 429s?
sam_support: customers ACME, Brightline, & Nimbus reported errors. Support ticket #6543 opened and initial triage completed.
nikki_pm: noted. this affects hosted API hotpath for large-sequence gen; Dedicated customers might be affected if routed through the same pool. prioritizing enterprise outreach.
sre-jen: pulling autoscaler events: `autoscaler: scale request rejected: policy 'rate-tier-mapping' evaluation failed (403)` — rate service returned deny, preventing scale-op. chain reaction with tokenbucket denies.
leo_ops: can we force scale up GPU pool while we fix the policy? need to buy time.
sre-jen: yes initiating manual scale. patching HPA minReplicas to add capacity now:
```
kubectl -n inference patch hpa gpu-hotpath-pool-3 --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
```
deploy-bot: Deploy started: manual-scale-gpu-hotpath by sre-jen
sre-jen: manual scale succeeded, +2 nodes came up. queue depth dropped ~30% within 45s.
matt_almond: 429s decreased but still elevated — tokenbucket shows burst tokens stuck at 0 for many clients. I'm going to nudge rate-service config to temporarily restore burst refill.
sre-jen: agree but keep conservative for quota. plan: bump burst_refill to 50 r/s for 'standard' for 10m window and monitor.
matt_almond: applied patch to rate-config (hotpath):
```
PUT /rate-config/pools/hotpath
{ "tiers": { "standard": { "burst_refill": 50, "burst_capacity": 200 } } }
```
rate-service: config reload ok
matt_almond: immediate telemetry shows 429s drop 48% -> 12% in ~2min, tokenbank refilling.
nikki_pm: customer-impact update: 3 enterprise customers experienced degraded throughput/latency ~10-15m; CS alerted and offering SLA review.
sam_support: adding mitigation notes to tickets and notifying Customer Success leads.
leo_ops: root cause hypothesis: policy push unintentionally remapped many active client keys from 'burst' to 'standard' but with a zero/near-zero refill due to a default fallback. Autoscaler attempted to scale but rate-policy guard aborted scale requests when mapping failed, leaving pool starved. In short: misrouted tiers + restrictive guard + tokenbucket defaults = cascade.
sre-jen: immediate mitigations applied: 1) manual scale (HPA bump) 2) temp burst_refill bump for standard 3) enable targeted fallback routing to 'burst' for impacted client keys 4) rollback faulty rate-tier policy push.
matt_almond: initiating rollback of the problematic policy now.
deploy-bot: Rollback started by matt_almond
matt_almond: rollback complete. policy mapping restored to previous state.
sre-jen: monitoring: queue below threshold, 429s < 1% across hotpath.
nikki_pm: post-incident action items: - add CI/integration test for rate-tier mappings to catch mislabeling - add autoscaler bypass/override for critical pools when policy service returns errors - add alert that detects mass reassignment of clients across tiers - run a multi-service failure tabletop and update runbook
sre-jen: oncall handoff: handing to leo_ops in 20m. leaving play-by-play and commands used in this thread.
leo_ops: taking over. please paste any remaining logs and the exact commands you ran.
sre-jen: logs link: https://logs.internal/2098765432 (search index: gpu-hotpath-pool-3)
sre-jen: timeline summary: 20:10:14 alert fired -> 20:11:03 autoscaler scale op blocked by policy -> 20:12:10 manual HPA patch attempted -> 20:12:40 manual scale succeeded -> 20:15:22 rate-config bump applied -> 20:23:05 policy rollback -> 20:33:58 incident resolved. estimated customer impact window ~12 minutes.
leo_ops: ack. taking notes for postmortem and SLA outreach. tagging @product for SLA implications.
nikki_pm: thanks everyone — fast mitigation. :thumbsup: will coordinate customer comms with support.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: leo_ops.
